entities.summary: The Roman Period, spanning from approximately 31 BCE to 284 CE, marks the zenith of Roman power and influence following the tumultuous collapse of the Roman Republic. This era, a crucial sub-period within the broader Classical age, is fundamentally defined by the establishment of the Principate under Augustus and the subsequent consolidation of a vast imperial system. It is characterized by unprecedented political stability known as the Pax Romana, significant territorial expansion, and the widespread dissemination of Roman culture, law, and governance across three continents. This timeframe classification aligns with the Annals of the World Dewey-style system (division 923), emphasizing its foundational role in Western civilization.
